limits: Contract only: no registry implementation, repair patch, compiler output, new test result or live attachment.
Current one-start call graph supports owner retention; community_init has no internal one-shot guard.
Existing claim admission has no thread identity check and init flags are outside claim locking.
Legacy module-envelope visibility, volatile-written synchronization, handler reentrancy, signal safety and persistence remain unproved.
Later module envelopes may mask generated owners; generated lookup intentionally refines a generated-PC versus module-LR winner.
Actual target atomic code generation, code/cache publication ordering, native provenance/admission, writer/topology/recovery and activation ownership remain gates.
Ownership association does not establish fault causation, successful redirection, persisted blame or recovery.

proposed_contract.capacity: Reserve generated and inline target-ownership capacity before publication; no silent lost ownership
proposed_contract.core_result: Not a community blame ID; continues legacy LR/frame fallback
proposed_contract.later_module_policy: Module-first masking; no reverse loader admission or permanent non-overlap guarantee
proposed_contract.owner_custody: Explicit trusted owner kind and copied bounded identity; retained through failed init and restart requests
proposed_contract.ownership_extent: Exact generated instruction bytes; excludes literals, pool neighbors and allocation slack
proposed_contract.precedence: PC then LR then eligible frames; legacy module winner first at each address, generated community owner second
proposed_contract.publication: Invisible during fallible work; one irreversible publication after target unlock and before original/redirect
proposed_contract.reader: Bounded acquire of committed slots; no waiting, allocation, locks, callbacks or mutable-owner dereferences
proposed_contract.retention: Visible records, identity and code retained for process lifetime; close is not quiescence
